children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE Futures canola contracts were stronger on Thursday, closing just short of contract highs as gains in crude oil and the Chicago soy complex provided spillover support.
- November canola was up C$7.80 at C$839.30 per tonne.
- West Texas Intermediate climbed above US$100 per barrel and Chicago soybeans hit three-year highs.
- Forecasts calling for the chance of frost in northern reaches of the Canadian Prairies over the weekend were also supportive for canola.

- The United States Department of Agriculture will release updated supply/demand estimates on Friday and positioning ahead of the data accounted for some of the activity in the North American markets.
- Statistics Canada will release its first production estimates for 2026-27 on Sept. 16.
- There were 47,129 contracts traded on Thursday, which compares with Wednesday when 46,729 contracts changed hands. Spreading accounted for 23,786 of the contracts traded.
